text:
Maya: quick heads up, canary (web-ui) is showing chart stalls after today's deploy. sparklines freeze ~1.5-3s during interactions.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: web-ui v1.24.3 -> v1.24.4 (canary 10%) :rocket:

Alex: link to traces?

Maya: https://perf.redwood.corp/explore/trace/abc123
Network waterfall shows font preload + big bundle chunk around same time:
```
GET /assets/fonts/graph-font.woff2  120ms
GET /assets/chunk-analytics.9876.js  240ms
LongTask main-thread 1800ms
```

Sasha: did the chunk hash change? might be invalidating existing prefetched chunks -> double download / main thread parsing.

Zach: here's a console sample:
```
[LongTask] start 167ms duration 1623ms
 at parseAndInstantiate (chunk-analytics.9876.js:45)
 at renderSparklines (sparklines.tsx:82)
```

Irene: telemetry sampler spike + routing fanout could be adding CPU when we fan out trace events to collector. If the sampler went from 0.05 -> 0.5 in the same deploy that could explain the bump.

Alex: can we short-circuit: 1) revert font preload 2) lower telemetry sampler 3) disable chunk prefetch for canary

Maya: ran quick experiment: disabling "<link rel=\"preload\" as=\"font\">" in canary -> stall drops from ~2.1s -> ~300-400ms on median. Reverting the font preload seems to help.

Zach: interesting — so font decode/parsing blocks main thread while chunk eval also happens. If both coincide we get the big longtask. Maybe move font decode off main thread (font-display: swap) and defer heavy chunk evals.

Sasha: purging CDN for chunk-analytics and forcing new chunk upload to stable hashes. triggering purge now. @deploy-bot can we push a micro-rollout that disables preload?

deploy-bot: starting rollout: web-ui v1.24.5 (canary) -> config change: font-preload=false, telemetry_sampler=0.05

Maya: rolling. i'll monitor perf dashboards and telemetry. thanks all :thumbsup:

Sasha: cdn purge done. will follow up if any 404s.

Alex: follow-up actions: add a test to simulate font preload + chunk eval concurrency, add guard in loader to stagger parse. Also add a telemetry check to alert if sampler changed >2x during deploys.

Maya: noted. I'll open RFC and assign tasks.

Zach: re-open if we see any regression after canary to 100%.
